capabilities.title: Painting supports, seams and brim
capabilities.note: Placement comes from settings, not from the mouse: supports from support_material and its threshold angle, seams from seam_position, brim from brim_type and brim_width.

capabilities.title: Text embossing and font loading
capabilities.note: A mesh with the text already in it is an ordinary object; the engine reads no fonts and places no glyphs.
capabilities.instead: any STL, 3MF or OBJ that carries the embossing

capabilities.title: Cut and hollow
capabilities.note: The engine slices a closed mesh; it never subtracts, splits or shells one. A cut or hollowed body has to arrive that way.

capabilities.title: STEP and IGES import
capabilities.note: B-rep to triangle needs an OCCT-class kernel, which is a dependency this project will not take. Nothing here reads a parametric solid.

capabilities.title: Resin (SLA/DLP) slicing
capabilities.note: The pipeline is filament: extrusion per bead, retraction, a layer cooling rule. Resin wants exposure per layer and no extrusion.

capabilities.title: Multi-material colour mixing (MMU, AMS)
capabilities.note: A tool changer is in scope and a colour mixer is not: beads are assigned to tools, never blended within one layer.

capabilities.title: Nesting arranger
capabilities.note: The arranger is a shelf packer: it fills rows, it does not interlock irregular outlines. It falls back to turning a part a quarter turn.

settings.name: avoid_crossing_perimeters
settings.hfw: avoid_crossing_perimeters — on by default: the emitter routes the travel itself around the loops — the layer's perimeters are offset both ways by a bead of clearance, and a visibility graph over those offset rings yields a path that holds that clearance from every wall, emitted as one retracted chain of moves. A closed loop keeps the seam the profile chose unless the seam is `nearest`, so routing costs distance and never the seam; only an open path has its entry point moved to save the crossing. Partial because supports and curled overhangs from earlier layers are not obstacles, and a travel whose start or end sits against several nested walls can find no route at all and falls back to the straight move

settings.name: avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour
settings.hfw: avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour — caps both the entry-point choice and the routed travel: a route longer than the straight move plus this budget is refused and the straight move is emitted instead. Zero means no limit, so the shipped profiles route without a ceiling

settings.name: elefant_foot_compensation
settings.hfw: elefant_foot_compensation — shrinks the first layer's cross-section by the value, on the printed outline, so walls, infill, skin and the brim all follow the compensated layer. The offset is taken on the whole region at once, so a hole smaller than twice the value closes instead of turning inside out. Where the offset merges or opens a feature is decided on a grid of one third of the value (0.02 mm floor), and every vertex is then walked onto the exact offset from the contour it came from

settings.name: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_positive
settings.hfw: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_positive — solved per bead path against the widest section on it, so a widening bead cannot push its own rate past the cap and a narrowing one pays its wide end's price. What is not done is what upstream does: splitting the move, so that two beads of different width meeting at a path boundary cannot step the rate between them. Measured on taper_wall, that boundary step reaches 6.2 mm3/s2 against a 4 mm3/s2 cap

settings.name: slice_closing_radius
settings.hfw: slice_closing_radius — fills cracks narrower than twice the value and drops holes smaller than it, on the sliced cross-section before compensation or simplification. Implemented by pulling the two boundary pieces together onto their midpoint rather than by an offset and back in, so a layer without a crack is left bit-identical instead of carrying a grid's error; the cost is that a concave corner is not rounded by the radius the way upstream's closing rounds it

settings.name: top_fill_pattern
settings.hfw: top_fill_pattern — all eight patterns are drawn: the five straight and concentric ones from this engine's own fill, and hilbertcurve, archimedeanchords and octagramspiral from upstream's plane-path curves clipped to the skin mask. monotonic and monotoniclines share one geometry because this engine's emitter decides the joining, not the fill

settings.name: top_infill_extrusion_width
settings.hfw: top_infill_width — the top skin is drawn with its own bead width while the shell layers under it keep the solid width

settings.name: wall_distribution_count
settings.hfw: wall_distribution_count — spreads the difference between the outer loop's width and the inner ones over the band with upstream's parabolic weights, centred on the middle loop. This engine's beading already places each bead from the geometry through the medial axis, so the only difference it has to distribute is that outer-width one; one loop is the default and reproduces the undistributed band exactly

settings.name: xy_size_compensation
settings.hfw: xy_size_compensation — grows the object and closes its holes when positive, shrinks it and opens them when negative, on every layer, through the same whole-region offset as the elephant-foot correction. Applied to the sliced cross-section rather than to the mesh, which is where PrusaSlicer applies it too, so the layer height schedule is unaffected
